Language.String: Volumetric Weather could not draw its clouds on this computer, so it has switched itself off: nothing in this city is changed by it.\n\n The mod needs Metal or OpenGL 3.3, and the game does not have either here. If the game is started with a launch option that changes its graphics (Steam: right-click the game, Properties, Launch Options), remove it and restart the game.

Volumetric Weather could not draw its clouds on this computer, so it has switched itself off: nothing in this city is changed by it.

 The mod needs OpenGL 3.3, and the game does not have it here. If the game is started with a launch option that changes its graphics (Steam: right-click the game, Properties, Launch Options), remove it and restart the game.

 The Windows version of the game runs the mod through Proton: Steam, right-click the game, Properties, Compatibility, tick "Force the use of a specific Steam Play compatibility tool" and pick a Proton version.

Volumetric Weather could not draw its clouds on this PC, so it has switched itself off: nothing in this city is changed by it.

 The usual causes:
 - the game is started with a launch option such as -force-d3d9, or -force-glcore on a graphics card whose OpenGL is older than 3.3 (Steam: right-click the game, Properties, Launch Options). Remove it, and restart the game.
 - the graphics card is older than DirectX 10.

 If neither applies, please report it in the comments on the mod's Workshop page, with this file:
 {0}

Mac and Linux support is new and experimental: expect a lower frame rate than on a Windows PC. If the game stutters, pick the Low quality preset on the in-game panel's Rendering tab (switch on the advanced options above to see it), or lower the game's resolution.
Follow the game's weather (clear every override)
Turns off all three overrides below at once, so the clouds, fog and lightning go back to following the game's weather.
Following the game: {0} -> intensity {1} (clear {2} to rain {3})
Set the amount of cloud yourself with the slider below, whatever the game's weather is doing. Only the clouds change: rain, fog and lightning still follow the game.
How much of the sky is covered in cloud. Even at 100% a few gaps stay open, so some sunlight still gets through.
How fast the clouds drift across the sky. They stop when the game is paused and speed up with the game speed.
Volumetric fog: waiting for the clouds
Set the amount of fog yourself with the slider below. When off, the fog follows the game's foggy weather, or another mod's fog setting.
How much of the map is covered in fog: 30% is about a third of it, 100% is everywhere.
Choose how often lightning flashes with the slider below, for example for a dry thunderstorm. When off, it follows the rain. This lightning is only for show: it never starts fires.
How often lightning flashes. Even at the top of the slider, rapid flickering is held back to protect players who are sensitive to flashing lights.
Test lightning (visual only, in front of the camera)
Shows one lightning strike in front of the camera, taking turns between a bolt to the ground and a flash inside the cloud. Works while the game is paused.
Shows the clouds. When off, you get the game's normal sky back, and this mod's cloud shadows, rain, fog and lightning are switched off with them.
How high the bottom of the clouds is, above sea level.
How tall the clouds are, from bottom to top. Taller clouds are darker underneath and cost a little more performance.
How torn the clouds are. Low gives smooth, solid clouds; high gives ragged clouds with more gaps between them.
The size of that tearing: low breaks off big chunks, high makes fine wisps.

Small, thin shreds of cloud around the big clouds, the ragged pieces real skies have between and beside their large clouds. The number is how much of the sky they cover; at 0 there are none. They need some open sky to show: at a very high intensity the big clouds leave no room for them.
How the fragments look. Clustered: gathered around the edges of the big clouds. Scattered: spread over the sky in random patches. Wispy: scattered too, but thinner, fainter and more torn.
Colour (white leaves the clouds as they are)

The colour of the light on the clouds' sunny side: their tops, the sides facing the sun and the bright rim around them (the moon's light at night). Only the colour changes: how bright the clouds are stays with the brightness settings. White leaves them as they are.

The colour of the clouds' shaded side: their undersides and the sides away from the sun, lit by the sky. At night it also colours the faint glow under the clouds, which over a city is often orange. Only the colour changes: how bright the clouds are stays with the brightness settings. White leaves them as they are.
Type or paste a colour and press Enter: #FFC0CB, rgb(255, 192, 203), 255, 192, 203, or a name such as pink.
Copy this colour ({0}) to the clipboard.
Use the colour on the clipboard: #FFC0CB, rgb(255, 192, 203), 255, 192, 203, or a name such as pink.
Back to white: the clouds' own colour, as without this setting.

Real 3D fog that lies on the land: it has a top you can see from above, and sunbeams break through it. It replaces the game's foggy-weather effect; the game's distance haze stays. This is by far the most demanding setting in the mod.
WARNING: This setting will significantly impact performance. Only recommended for users with powerful hardware.

Volumetric fog is by far the heaviest thing this mod draws and can cost a large part of your frame rate, most of all with the camera down in it.

 The game's own fog keeps working if you leave this off.

 Turn it on?
Fog lit by the city's lights
At night, fog around street lamps, buildings and car headlights glows in the colour of their light. Only works with volumetric fog on.
How thick the fog is, which decides how far you can see through it. Thicker fog can cost more performance.
Off: the fog is flat, like a lake of fog, so valleys fill up and hills rise out of it. On: the fog lies evenly over the land and follows hills and mountains.
How high the bottom of the fog is: above sea level, or above the ground when the fog follows it. 0 starts the fog at the bottom. Raise it for fog that only hangs higher up, like low cloud.
How thick the fog layer is, from its bottom to its top. For example, starting at 200 m with a height of 150 m gives fog from 200 m to 350 m.
How patchy the fog is. Low gives solid fog; high gives thin, wispy fog with gaps.
How fast the fog drifts and swirls. 0 keeps it still.
How bright the fog looks. This is separate from the brightness of the clouds.
Gives the fog a cold blue-grey or a warm, hazy tint. The time of day still colours it too: orange at sunset, blue at night.

Any colour for the fog, on top of the tint above and the light it stands in. Only the colour changes: how bright the fog is stays with 'Fog brightness'. White leaves it as it is. The glow of the city's lights inside the fog keeps the lights' own colours.
How brightly the city's lights make the fog around them glow.
How far the glow reaches from each light before it fades away.
How the game's weather maps to cloud cover
How much cloud there is on a clear day. Raise it for more cloud in good weather. The game's weather still moves the sky between this and the rain setting below.
How much cloud there is when it rains, or when the game's weather turns cloudy. Raise it for darker, more dramatic storms.
How big the cloud patterns are. Smaller gives more, smaller groups of clouds across the map; larger gives big, sweeping weather systems.
Rain falls only under the thickest clouds, in curtains you can see from far away, instead of the game's rain that follows the camera everywhere. How much it rains is still up to the game.
How thick the rain looks from a distance, under the clouds. 0 leaves only the raindrops near the camera.
How many raindrops fall past the camera. 0 leaves only the rain you see from a distance.
Above this camera height the nearby raindrops fade away. From high up you see the rain from a distance instead.
How long each raindrop's streak is. Longer streaks read as faster, heavier rain; shorter ones as drops.
How thick each streak is. Streaks too thin to see from far away fade out rather than flicker.
How visible the streaks are against the scene. 0 hides them; higher makes them stand out.
A tint for the streaks. Their colour already follows the sky, darker at night and warmer at sunset; this only changes the hue. White leaves them as they are.
How fast the rain falls. It also moves the rain curtains in the distance, so both stay in step. Slow rain with short, wide, bright streaks looks like sleet.
Rain sound and wet roads follow the clouds
You only hear rain, and roads only get wet, where it is actually raining, so it stays dry where the sky is clear.
Lightning lights the clouds and rain
Lightning lights up the clouds and rain from inside. This also adds extra lightning in storms, which is only for show and never starts fires.
Draws a new, different bolt each time, coming down from the clouds, instead of the game's single fixed bolt. Thunder and fires work as before.
How bright the lightning bolt and its flash in the clouds are.
How much lightning heavy rain brings. At 100% there is about one strike every three seconds in the heaviest rain.
Clouds cast shadows on the ground
Clouds cast moving shadows on the city. This is the only thing in the mod that darkens the ground.
How dark the ground gets under thick cloud. Gaps between the clouds always get full sunlight.
Makes thin clouds and cloud edges cast stronger shadows, so more of the ground is shaded. Raise it if the shadows look too faint.
How brightly the clouds are lit
Clouds are brighter in fair weather and greyer when they fill the sky, between the two settings below. Turn it off to use one fixed brightness instead.
How bright the clouds are when there are only a few of them.
How bright the clouds are when they cover the whole sky.
The cloud brightness used when 'Brightness follows the cloud intensity' is off.
Clouds dim at full overcast to
How much the clouds darken as they fill the sky. Only used when 'Brightness follows the cloud intensity' is off.
How thick and solid the clouds look. Higher makes them whiter on top and darker underneath.
Clouds hide the stars at night
Stops stars from showing through the clouds at night. It has no effect during the day.
Glow under the clouds at night
A soft, pale glow on the underside of the clouds at night, like the light a city throws up into the sky.
Sets the three performance settings below in one go. Lower it if the mod costs you too many frames. Changing any of those three yourself switches this to Custom.
How much detail goes into drawing the clouds and the fog. The first thing to lower on a slower graphics card: halving it roughly halves what they cost.
How sharp the cloud shadows are. Lower it to gain frames; what it costs does not depend on your screen resolution.
How many times a second the cloud shadows are updated. Lower is faster, but the shadows move a little less smoothly.
Buildings and terrain hide clouds behind them
Hills and buildings in front of a cloud hide it, as they should. Only turn this off if something looks wrong where the clouds meet the scenery.

Replaces the game's glow around street lamps, building lights and vehicle lights with this mod's own, which the settings below control. Like the game's, it grows in foggy weather (the game's fog, or Play It!'s fog slider). It also fixes the white squares the game sometimes draws around lights. Off leaves the game's lights exactly as they are.
Higher keeps the bright centre of each glow and removes the wide haze around it, so lights look smaller and crisper.
How bright the glow around lights is. With a high tightness you may need to raise this to see the glow at all.
How far the glow spreads around each light. Lights close to the camera can be adjusted separately below.
The same lamps, close to the camera
Lights closer to the camera than this use the three settings below, blending back to normal by twice this distance. 0 turns this off.
The tightness of nearby lights, as a percentage of the tightness above.
The brightness of nearby lights, as a percentage of the brightness above. Below about 100% a tight glow fades out quickly.
The size of nearby lights' glow, as a percentage of the size above. This is the one that shrinks a big blob of light right in front of the camera.
How bright the glow around vehicle lights and other moving lights is. Lamps placed with Intersection Marking Tool use the street lamp settings instead.
Two older settings for vehicle lights: how far their glow reaches, and hiding the glow of lights very close to the camera.
How far the glow of vehicle lights reaches. 100% is the game's normal size.
Vehicle lights closer to the camera than this have no glow. 0 turns this off.
Language (more languages are coming soon; for now it is English only)
The language of this mod's panels, tooltips and settings file. 'Same as the game' follows the game's own language. The in-game panel switches at once, this options page the next time you open it.
The in-game panel (every setting of the sky is there)
The key that opens and closes the in-game panel. Click, then press the new key. Backspace clears it; Escape cancels.
Show advanced options in the in-game panel

Adds four more tabs to the in-game panel -- Weather, Light, Rendering and Halos -- with every other setting of the mod: how the game's weather maps to the sky, shadows and brightness, performance, and the street-light glow.
Puts this mod's button in the Unified UI bar. Without Unified UI, the button sits on its own in the corner of the screen instead.
Writes much more detail to VolumetricClouds.log. Leave it off normally. To report a problem: turn it on, make the problem happen, then send the log.
Puts every setting back to how the mod comes. This also turns off 'Volumetric fog' and 'Show advanced options in the in-game panel'.

Put every setting back to how the mod comes?\n\n This throws away everything you have tuned, including changes made in the in-game panel, and turns off 'Volumetric fog' and 'Show advanced options in the in-game panel'.
Gives this city a new arrangement of clouds and fog. A city keeps its sky in its save, so this is how you get a different one. None of your settings change. Only works with a city loaded.

Give this city a new pattern of clouds and fog?

 Your last save keeps the old one until you, or the autosave, save again: loading it before then brings the old sky back.

 None of your settings change.
The mod's button (without Unified UI): distance from the left edge
The mod's button (without Unified UI): distance from the top edge

Volumetric Weather settings.
 
 You can edit this file while the game is running: the mod reads it again within a second of it being saved, and the panels follow.
 
 - Numbers use a dot for decimals: 0.5, never 0,5.
 - A percentage is written the way its slider shows it: 47 means 47%.
 - A value outside its range is pulled back into it. A value that cannot be read, and a name the mod does not know, are ignored. VolumetricClouds.log says which.
 - A setting whose line is missing keeps the value it has (at startup, its default).
 - If the file cannot be read at all, the mod leaves it alone and says so in the log.
 - The mod rewrites this file, these comments included, whenever a setting changes in the game: notes of your own will not survive.
 - Delete the file with the game closed to start again from every default.
In-game panel, with advanced options on: {0} tab
{0}. A key such as F4 or Ctrl+Shift+C, or None; default {1}.
{0}. A colour, #RRGGBB (255, 192, 203 is read too); default {1}.
Switching it on here skips the question the game asks first.
